summary: The admitted stoned-clay case reached polyself.c:polymon's active-stoning branch, where JavaScript threw because the already-implemented poly_when_stoned helper was not imported.

source.branch: Upstream polyself.c:polymon (735-1071) checks Stoned && poly_when_stoned(&mons[mntmp]); when the helper approves the target form, it selects PM_STONE_GOLEM and calls make_stoned in source order.
source.javascript: js/polyself.js:polymon already mirrors this branch, but the named import list omitted poly_when_stoned exported by js/mondata.js, causing a ReferenceError at the branch.
callers: cmd.c:doextcmd #polyself -> wizcmds.c:wiz_polyself -> polyself.c:polyself -> polyself.c:polymon; js/cmd.js:runPolyselfCommand -> js/wizcmds.js:wiz_polyself -> js/polyself.js:polyself -> polymon
dependencies: The existing js/mondata.js poly_when_stoned implementation is used without behavior changes.
source.resolution: Add the existing poly_when_stoned helper to polyself.js's named imports and pin the source guard and import in scripts/polyself.test.mjs.

evidence: The admitted v70 evaluation reports 0/169 screens matched and ReferenceError: poly_when_stoned is not defined in polyself.c:polymon at step 116.

Upstream polyself.c:polymon checks Stoned with poly_when_stoned(&mons[mntmp]); when approved it sets PM_STONE_GOLEM and calls make_stoned. The JavaScript branch already had this order; the missing named import was the defect.
After the import, the focused bounded scan matched all 169/169 screens, RNG calls, cursors, and the input boundary through segment 0 step 168. No unported callees were reached.
